title: Viva Engage: apply Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to communities
summary: Hold pending a correction to the testing guidance: new container labels configured with Teams shared channel controls require at least 24 hours, not the briefing's unqualified one-hour wait. The roadmap facts, licensing quotations and control commands are supported; several paths stop before the final setting, and two Microsoft pages give conflicting guidance on changes to existing labels.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Community creators and community admins can manually apply sensitivity labels to Engage communities.
claims.quote: Community admins can change the sensitivity label (and hence its privacy setting) of a community. ... The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.claim: Labels can be applied to communities after labels and associated policies are configured in Purview.
claims.quote: After you configure sensitivity labels with their associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, these labels can be applied to communities in your organization.

claims.quote: Admins can set up sensitivity labels to automatically apply during community creation. When a user creates a new community, the default sensitivity label automatically applies to the community.

claims.claim: The community creator can choose a different label from those available to them.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.claim: Community creators cannot create new sensitivity labels through this choice.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.claim: Public or Private label privacy sets and locks the community's privacy until the sensitivity label is removed.
claims.quote: The settings of Public or Private set and lock the privacy setting when you apply this label to the container. ... locks the privacy value so it can be changed only by first removing the sensitivity label from the container.

claims.claim: Public label privacy allows anyone in the organisation to access the community container.
claims.quote: Privacy: Keep the default of Public if you want anyone in your organization to access the container where this label is applied.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[4]; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A community created with a label disallowing guest access is available only to internal users and outside people cannot be added.
claims.quote: Communities created with a label that doesn’t allow guest access are only available to users in your organization. People outside your organization can’t be added to the community.

claims.claim: Items inside labelled containers do not inherit the container label's markings or encryption.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[4].note; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Changing External users access applies to new users, not existing guests, who retain access.
claims.quote: The new setting applies to new users but not to existing users. ... these guest users can still access the site after this setting is cleared in the label configuration.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enabled and configured container labels can be seen and applied on team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Engage communities and Loop workspaces.
claims.quote: After you enable and configure sensitivity labels for containers, users can additionally see and apply sensitivity labels to containers that support them. These include Microsoft team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces.

claims.where: controls[1]; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: EnableMIPLabels is the tenant-level Microsoft Entra group setting used to enable container label support.
claims.quote: To apply published labels to groups, you must first enable the feature. These steps enable the feature in Microsoft Entra ID. ... If the sensitivity label was enabled previously, you see EnableMIPLabels = True.

claims.claim: Container sensitivity label support is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: If you haven't yet enabled sensitivity labels for containers, do the following set of steps as a one-time procedure: ... follow the instructions from the Microsoft Entra documentation to enable sensitivity label support

claims.claim: In a tenant without enabled container labels, community labelling requires enabling support, synchronising labels and publishing a Groups & sites label.
claims.quote: Until sensitivity labels are enabled for containers, the settings are visible but you can't configure them. ... make sure you select Groups & sites for the label's scope ... If your sensitivity label isn't already published, now publish it

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; controls[3].ui; controls[4].ui; Governance controls
claims.claim: Labels for community container protection require the Groups & sites scope.
claims.quote: The Groups & sites scope becomes available and selected by default when you enable sensitivity labels for containers and synchronize labels. This option lets you protect content in SharePoint sites, Teams sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces by labeling those containers

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell synchronises the labels to Microsoft Entra ID after enabling support.
claims.quote: You now need to synchronize your sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra ID. First, connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... Then run the following command to ensure your sensitivity labels can be used with Microsoft 365 groups: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync

claims.claim: The Engage documentation describes using a more permissive community default alongside a more restrictive SharePoint site default.
claims.quote: Create a more permissive default for Engage communities, while maintaining a more restrictive default for sites.

claims.claim: Purview recommends first publishing a configured container label to a policy covering a few test users.
claims.quote: After you create and configure the sensitivity label, add this label to a label policy that applies to just a few test users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Purview's testing guidance is to wait at least one hour for a new Groups & sites label, without a configuration exception.
claims.quote: New label: Wait at least one hour, unless your configured settings include Teams shared channel controls. If that's the case, wait at least 24 hours.
claims.fix: In both occurrences, replace the new-label timing with: 'Wait at least one hour for a new label, or at least 24 hours if its configured settings include Teams shared channel controls; wait at least 24 hours for an existing label.' This retains the qualification for labels also used by Teams.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Purview says changes to an existing container label take at least 24 hours to replicate before testing.
claims.quote: Existing label: Wait at least 24 hours. ... If you do, remember to wait at least 24 hours for the changes to replicate to all containers that have the label applied.
claims.fix: Add: 'The Entra group-label documentation instead says changes to published group settings are not automatically applied to labelled groups and recommends manually reapplying updates with its linked PowerShell script.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/users/groups-assign-sensitivity-labels#group-setting-changes-to-published-labels-arent-updated-on-the-groups alongside the Purview timing.

claims.claim: Purview warns that deleting a container label still included in a policy can cause new team, group and site creation failures.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label that has the site and group settings enabled, and that label is included in one or more label policies, this action can result in creation failures for new teams, groups, and sites.
claims.fix: Add: 'The general label-creation documentation says a label cannot be deleted while it is still in a label policy.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels#removing-and-deleting-labels. Retain the existing remove-first advice.

claims.claim: Removing a container label from every publishing policy and waiting at least one hour are steps before deleting it.
claims.quote: Remove the sensitivity label from all label policies that include the label. Wait at least one hour.

claims.quote: As a workaround, you can use PowerShell to apply labels to a SharePoint site that connects to an existing Engage community. Doing so causes the label on the Engage community to correspondingly update.

claims.quote: This tenant-level setting can be changed by Microsoft Entra Global Administrator or Microsoft Entra Yammer Administrator (Viva Engage admin).

Enabling uses Graph PowerShell; Entra UI procedures assign labels to groups rather than enable the tenant feature.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -AddLabels "<label>" adds the identified sensitivity label to the policy.
claims.quote: The AddLabels parameter specifies the sensitivity labels that you want to add to the policy. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the label. For example: Name Distinguished name (DN) GUID

claims.claim: The modern Purview label creation route through Groups & sites and Privacy and external user access settings reaches privacy configuration.

The opening modern-scheme steps are supported by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels; the current docs URL supplies the final configuration steps.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity "<label>" -SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy Private sets label privacy, whose valid values are Public and Private.
claims.quote: The SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy parameter specifies the privacy level for the labe. Valid values are: Public Private

claims.claim: The modern Purview label creation route through Groups & sites and Privacy and external user access settings reaches guest-access configuration.

The opening modern-scheme steps are supported by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels; the current docs URL supplies the final configuration steps.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity "<label>" -SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers $false disables guest access in the label.
claims.quote: The SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers parameter enables or disables access to guest users. Valid values are: $true: Guest access is enabled. $false: Guest access is disabled.

claims.claim: The Engage documentation does not state the new-community label outcome when no Engage default is configured.

claims.claim: The checklist's distinct Engage default-label decision has no corresponding control row.
claims.quote: Decide which label new communities get by default ... default label for Engage communities ... | controls[2]: Which sensitivity labels a label policy publishes to its users and groups; note mentions Apply this label by default to groups and sites.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Decide which label new communities get by default, using the default label for Engage communities in the label policy that the Engage page describes.' Keep the supported default-label explanation in the body; do not add a row.

claims.claim: Set-Label and Set-LabelPolicy run in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can now use Security & Compliance PowerShell to create and configure all the settings you see in your labeling admin center. ... See the following documentation for supported parameters and values: New-Label New-LabelPolicy Set-Label Set-LabelPolicy

claims.claim: Purview recommends avoiding changes to a label's site and group settings after it has been applied.
claims.quote: As a best practice, don't change the site and group settings for a sensitivity label after the label has been applied to teams, groups, or sites.
